key_insight: UniAIR is a unified multimodal AI framework that predicts the functional effects of mutations across antibodies, antigens and T cell receptors using a single, generalizable model — enabling cross-modal transfer of mutation-effect knowledge.
problem_solved: Existing predictors are often modality-specific (antibody-only, antigen-only or TCR-only), which limits cross-task generalization and requires separate models and datasets; UniAIR addresses the need for a single model that generalizes mutation-effect prediction across diverse adaptive immune recognition contexts.
method: Unified multimodal architecture that jointly represents sequence and structural information from antibodies, antigens and TCRs into a shared embedding space.
Mutation-aware scoring head trained via cross-modal pretraining and task-specific fine-tuning to predict the functional impact of single and combinatorial mutations.
Leveraging diverse labeled and unlabeled immune interaction data to improve transferability and robustness across recognition settings.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, UniAIR demonstrates that a single multimodal model can replace multiple specialized predictors, improving sample efficiency and enabling transferable mutation-effect models useful for protein engineering, vaccine design and interpretability research.
visual_elements: Schematic diagram of the unified architecture showing separate encoders (antibody, antigen, TCR) feeding into a shared embedding space and a mutation-effect scoring head.
Heatmap or sequence-logo style visualization of predicted mutation effects across a protein region (before vs after mutation).
Bar/line chart comparing UniAIR performance to modality-specific baselines across antibody, antigen and TCR benchmarks.
Workflow icon set: data sources → multimodal pretraining → fine-tuning → mutation-effect predictions (deployment use-cases: design, screening).
paper_title: Generalizable mutation-effect prediction across adaptive immune recognition via unified multimodal framework
paper_authors: Rong Han, Yumeng Zhang, Xiaohong Liu, Lei Fu, Tong Pan
